verses.text: The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people who had come back from being prisoners were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel.

So they came to Zerubbabel and the family leaders and said, "Let us help you build, because we worship your God just as you do. We have been offering sacrifices to him since the time of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the other family leaders of Israel answered, "You have no part with us in building a temple for our God. We alone will build it for the LORD, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, commanded us."
Then the people of the land tried to discourage the people of Judah and make them afraid to build.
They paid advisers to work against them and stop their plans. They did this the whole time Cyrus was king of Persia, until Darius became king of Persia.
At the beginning of the rule of Xerxes, they wrote an accusation against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
In the time of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their friends wrote a letter to Artaxerxes king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic letters and in the Aramaic language.
Rehum the commanding officer and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes. It said this.
It was from Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the secretary, and their friends: the judges, officials, and leaders over the people from Erech, Babylon, Susa in Elam, and other places,
and the other peoples whom the great and famous Ashurbanipal moved and settled in the city of Samaria and in other places west of the Euphrates River.
This is a copy of the letter they sent: "To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the people west of the Euphrates River.
The king should know that the Jews who came up from you to us have gone to Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and evil city. They are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.
The king should know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, they will stop paying taxes, payments, and fees, and the king's income will suffer.
Since we are loyal to the palace, we do not want to see the king dishonored. So we are sending to tell the king,

so that you can search the record books of your ancestors. In those books you will find that this city is a rebellious city that has caused trouble for kings and provinces. It has been a place of rebellion since long ago. That is why it was destroyed.
We are telling the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will have nothing left west of the Euphrates River."
Then the king sent this answer: "To Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the secretary, and their friends living in Samaria and in the rest of the land west of the Euphrates River: Greetings.
The letter you sent us has been translated and read to me.
I gave an order, and a search was made. It was found that this city has rebelled against kings since long ago. It has been a place of rebellion and revolt.
Powerful kings have ruled over Jerusalem and all the land west of the Euphrates River, and taxes, payments, and fees were paid to them.
So now give an order to make these men stop. This city must not be rebuilt until I give the order.
Be careful not to neglect this. Why let this danger grow and harm the kings?"
As soon as a copy of King Artaxerxes' letter was read to Rehum, Shimshai the secretary, and their friends, they hurried to the Jews in Jerusalem and forced them to stop.
So the work on God's temple in Jerusalem stopped. It stayed stopped until the second year of the rule of Darius king of Persia.
